summary: Describes the NOPEER BGP community, a well-known advisory attribute with which an origin AS asks that a route need not be passed across bilateral peering connections. It gives a way to control how far a route spreads. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A network can attach a tag to its route saying, no need to pass this around to your friends, only to your customers.

subtitle: Control how far a route spreads across networks.

tldr.problem: Networks need a way to prevent specific routes from being propagated beyond a certain scope, especially to limit how far more specific routes travel when they are only useful locally.
tldr.mechanism: The NOPEER community is a BGP attribute that an origin network attaches to a route to advise remote networks not to re-advertise it across bilateral peer connections, limiting its spread to customer relationships only.
tldr.outcome: Routes marked with NOPEER stop at peering boundaries, reducing unnecessary global route table growth while still allowing transit providers to pass them to customers.

facts.label: Route table growth
facts.value: More than 51% of table is more-specific routes

today: RFC 3765 is an Internet Standard and defines the NOPEER community in active use in BGP networks. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: What NOPEER Does
sections.content:
The NOPEER community is a well-known BGP attribute that allows a network to control how its route prefixes spread through the internet. When an origin network includes this community on a specific route, it is asking other networks not to re-advertise that route to bilateral peer connections; the route can still be advertised to customer networks.

This document describes the NOPEER community, why it is useful, and how networks should interpret it. NOPEER is an advisory mechanism—networks that receive routes with this attribute can choose to suppress redistribution to their peers.
sections.eli5: NOPEER is a tag on a route that asks: 'don't pass this to your friends, but it's okay to pass it to your customers.' Networks can use it to control where their routes go.

sections.title: How NOPEER Works
sections.content:
The NOPEER community is defined as a well-known transitive BGP community with the value 0xFFFFFF04. It travels with the route across multiple networks and allows each network to interpret it independently.

When a network receives a route marked with NOPEER, it should not re-advertise that route to its bilateral peers—networks where neither side is a customer of the other. However, the network can advertise the route to providers and customers. This distinction between peering (bilateral) and customer relationships is the key to NOPEER's operation.
sections.eli5: NOPEER is like a flag that rides along with the route. Each network that sees it can decide not to pass it to their peers, but can still give it to their customers and providers.

sections.title: Why Networks Use NOPEER
sections.content:
A common routing practice is for a network to advertise both a broad aggregate route (like 10.0.0.0/23) and more specific prefixes within it (like 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24). The more specific routes help with traffic engineering and local optimization—steering traffic to the right place within the network. However, these more specific routes are only useful near the origin; once traffic is far away, it cannot make any finer routing decisions and just follows the aggregate.

When more specific routes spread globally anyway, they contribute to route table bloat—the BGP routing table was already growing at over 10% per year. About 51% of the routing table consists of more specific routes that do not add actual reachability, just finer detail that is not universally needed. NOPEER allows the origin network to tell remote networks that these specific routes need not be passed to bilateral peers, controlling unnecessary propagation.
sections.eli5: Imagine a big building with lots of room numbers inside. You give a visitor the main address and also the room numbers, but room numbers only matter if they're visiting that building. NOPEER says 'you don't need to tell your friends about our room numbers.'

sections.title: Security Risks
sections.content:
Although NOPEER is a simple advisory attribute, it introduces some security considerations. An attacker could add a NOPEER community to a route they do not own and cause that route to stop propagating, creating a denial of service against the target network. If the attacker injects a false more specific route without a covering aggregate and marks it with NOPEER, the false route might be suppressed at a peering boundary, making it harder to detect.

Additionally, NOPEER does not change BGP's fundamental vulnerability to route injection or modification attacks. It is an advisory attribute with no cryptographic protection. Networks must rely on other security mechanisms such as route filtering and RPKI to ensure that routes they receive are legitimate.
sections.eli5: NOPEER can be misused: someone could fake a NOPEER tag to make a real route disappear from view, or to hide a fake route they injected. BGP still needs other security tools to stay safe.
